answer: Beacon-tagged key derivation.** Each agent derives its signing key from a public randomness beacon plus its own fingerprint. Honest agents whose keys share an origin are detected when a periodic falcon scan reconciles derivation paths against the beacon transcript. Duplicating an identity forces the attacker onto a narrow ledge: every clone must re-derive keys and replay beacon proofs, paying a fresh derivation-plus-attestation cost per copy, while the shared transcript links the copies into one cluster that gets throttled collectively.
